content: The 2017 World Rapid Chess Championship was won by Levon Aronian [3]. Russian grandmaster Dmitry Andreikin won the gold medal in the men's rapid chess event of the IMSA Elite Mind Games in Huai'an, China in 2017 [2]. Former champion Vassily Ivanchuk of Ukraine won the 2016 World Rapid Championship [1] while Indian grandmaster Vishwanathan Anand is the current world rapid champion, having won the title on December 28, 2017 [5]. Shakhriyar Mamedyarov of Azerbaijan won the 2016 World Rapid Chess Championship, scoring 11½/15 [4].

The United States left the gold standard in March and April 1933 [3][4]. In doing so, the value of the dollar was allowed to float freely on foreign exchange markets with no guaranteed price in gold [5]. Before this transition, the dollar was technically worth exactly 1/35 of a troy ounce (889 mg) of gold [4].

The Svalbard Global Seed Vault was built between 2007 and 2008 [2][3][4]. The construction was funded by the Norwegian government and the facility officially opened on February 26, 2008 [2][3], although the first seeds arrived in January 2008 [2].

Patrick S. Castagne (1916-2000) is the composer of the national anthem of Trinidad and Tobago, "Forged from the Love of Liberty." He composed the anthem in 1962 while working for the Trinidad and Tobago Commission in London [1][2][3][4]. The anthem was originally composed as the national anthem for the West Indies Federation, which existed from 1958-1962, but was later adopted by Trinidad and Tobago after it gained independence in 1962 [1][3].

The famous street in New Orleans is Bourbon Street, a historic street in the heart of the French Quarter known for its many bars and strip clubs, having millions of visitors each year [1]. Another notable street is St. Charles Avenue, famous for its many mansions and tree-lined boulevard in the uptown section of the city [2]. Frenchmen Street is also well-known for its live music venues, restaurants, and other businesses in the Faubourg Marigny neighborhood [4]. Royal Street, while not quite as famous, is known for its antique shops, art galleries, and hotels, running through the French Quarter, Faubourg Marigny, Bywater, and Lower Ninth Ward neighborhoods [3, 5].

In the Beatles' song "Do You Want to Know a Secret" (1963), George Harrison is the lead singer [1][2]. According to John Lennon, he gave the song to Harrison because it suit his vocal range [2]. The song was written by Lennon-McCartney, but Lennon always claimed it as his own [2]. Billy J. Kramer and the Dakotas covered the song in 1964, and it reached No. 2 on the Billboard chart in the United States [1]. Alvin and the Chipmunks also covered the song in 1964, and it reached No. 1 on the Billboard chart in a cover version by Stars on 45 in 1981 [4].

The Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, which abolished slavery, was ratified by the required number of states on December 6, 1865 [2][3]. The ratification process was completed when North Carolina and Georgia gave the amendment the final votes needed for it to become part of the Constitution [1]. The Thirteenth Amendment became part of the Constitution on December 6, 1865 [1].

The song "Don't Matter to Me" by Drake featuring posthumous vocals from Michael Jackson was first released on July 6, 2018 as part of Drake's fifth studio album "Scorpion" [1]. The song reached number one in the United States, making it Drake's 31st top-ten song and Jackson's 30th top ten on the "Billboard" Hot 100, as well as being Jackson's second posthumous top-ten entry [2]. Michael Jackson recorded the vocals for "Don't Matter to Me" during an unreleased 1983 session with Canadian singer-songwriter Paul Anka [5]. It is unclear when Michael recorded "Don't Matter to Me" specifically.

England won the World Cup in soccer in 1966 during the 1966 FIFA World Cup, which was held in England from July 11 to July 30 [1][2][3][4]. The final match saw England win 4–2 over West Germany [1][2][3][4][5].

Washington is addressing both African Americans and white Southerners in the Atlanta Exposition, as he calls African Americans to join the workforce and emphasizes that the South provides opportunities for African Americans that are lacking in the North. He also appeals to the white audience not to rely on immigration as a solution to labor shortages, rather than encouraging African Americans to seek political and social equality [1][2][3][4][5].

Alabama became a right-to-work state in 1954 when it passed its first right-to-work law [1]. However, the law was repealed in 1956 [1]. The law was reinstituted in Louisiana in 1976 [2]. Alabama was not the first southern state to adopt such legislation, but it was one of the last [3].
The first North American Indigenous Games were held in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada in 1990 [1][2][3].

The Dark Tower series by Stephen King consists of eight main books: The Gunslinger, The Dark Tower, The Waste Lands, Wizard and Glass, Wolves of the Calla, Song of Susanna, The Dark Tower, and The Dark Tower VII: The Dark Tower [1][2][3][4][5]. Additionally, several of King's other books are tied to this series or reference it [1][2].

The Ferris wheel, called the Myrtle Beach SkyWheel, is located in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina [1][2]. It stands 187 feet tall, making it the tallest Ferris wheel in the United States east of the Mississippi River [1][2][3][4]. The wheel has 42 glass-enclosed, temperature-controlled gondolas, each with seating for six passengers [1]. The Myrtle Beach SkyWheel is situated near Plyler Park [2]. The wheel runs year-round, but high winds can necessitate removal of the gondolas for safety [2]. The Collins family planned and financed the construction of the SkyWheel, which began in 2011 [3].

Rick and Morty season 3 originally aired on Cartoon Network's adult-oriented late night programming block, Adult Swim [1][2]. The third season consisted of ten episodes and premiered on April 1, 2017, with the remaining episodes airing weekly, starting on July 30, 2017, on Adult Swim [1][2]. The episodes were available for free streaming on Adult Swim's website for the first two episodes, while subsequent episodes required a cable subscription to air the show live [2].

The term that refers to linking a currency value to the value of gold is known as the gold standard [1][2][3][4][5]. Under the gold standard, a country’s government declares that it will exchange its currency for a certain weight in gold [1][2]. In a pure gold standard, a country’s government declares that it will freely exchange currency for actual gold at the designated exchange rate [2]. A currency board is a monetary authority which is required to maintain a fixed exchange rate with a foreign currency, with gold standard being a special case of a currency board [4].

The first Olympic football (soccer) competition was held in 1900 [5]. Since then, it has been contested in every Summer Olympics except for 1904, 1906, 1932, and 1940. The 1928 edition was the last Olympic football tournament before the inception of the FIFA World Cup [3]. In 1984, the International Olympic Committee decided to admit professional players [4].

The Cleveland Browns returned to the NFL in 1999 after a three-year period of deactivation [1], [3]. The reactivated Browns' franchise was purchased by Lerner, a friend of former team owner Art Modell, after he outbid other interested parties [2]. The franchise is considered a continuation of the previous franchise, as the history and colors of the team remained in Cleveland [3]. Since resuming operations in 1999, the Browns have struggled to find success, having only had two winning seasons and one playoff appearance [1].

St. Petersburg is located in Pinellas County, Florida [1][3]. It is part of the larger Tampa Bay Area and is the fifth most populous city in Florida [1]. The St. Petersburg Library System serves the residents of the city of St. Petersburg [4].

The first hand-held camera was invented by Auguste and Louis Lumière in the 1890s [1]. The Lumière's Cinematograph could be used with a tripod or carried by the cameraman, and it served as the film projector as well [1]. In 1888, George Eastman introduced the first handheld amateur camera, the Kodak camera, which was marketed with the slogan "You press the button, we do the rest" [3]. The Kodak camera was easy to carry and use, making it accessible to a wider group of people.
Anne Hathaway plays the White Queen in Alice Through the Looking Glass (2010) [1][2]. Phyllis Diller portrayed the White Queen in the 1987 animated film Alice Through the Looking Glass [4][5].

The South Carolina Ordinance of Secession was drafted by a committee that included Christopher Memminger [1], William Henry Gist [2] and Francis Wilkinson Pickens [3]. The Ordinance was ratified by a special convention delegation on December 20, 1860 [2]. The text of the ordinance was not mentioned in any of the provided documents.

The total cost for Rio to host the 2016 Summer Olympics was estimated at USD 4.6 billion [1]. This cost included direct capital expenses for building competition venues, the Olympic village, international broadcast center, and media and press center [1]. The exorbitant cost compares with costs of USD 40-44 billion for Beijing 2008 and USD 51 billion for Sochi 2014, the most expensive Olympics in history [1, 5].

The winner of the final HoH in Big Brother 20 was Nick (also known as Nick Maccarone or "Macc Buchna") [1]. He emerged victorious in a 6-1 vote in the finale [1]. Additionally, in the pre-finale eviction, Nick evicted Tyler Crispen after winning the HoH competition [1].

The Gadsden Purchase, a territory of present-day southern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico, was bought by the United States from Mexico [1][5]. The Treaty, which took effect on June 8, 1854, was signed on December 30, 1853, by James Gadsden, U.S. ambassador to Mexico, and by President Antonio López de Santa Anna of Mexico [1][4].

The Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) was started on 15 May 1928 in Cloncurry, Queensland [1][2]. Before this, it was known as the Australian Inland Mission (AIM) Aerial Medical Service, which was a one-year experiment based in Cloncurry [1]. The RFDS continues to operate from various bases across Australia [4]. The first aircraft operated by the service was a de Havilland DH.50 hired from the fledgling Queensland and Northern Territory Aerial Service (Qantas) [4].

"Genie in a Bottle" is a song by Christina Aguilera, and it was released on June 22, 1999, as the lead single from her debut album [1]. The single charted highly and remained at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 for five consecutive weeks, becoming the biggest summer song of 1999 [2]. The success of "Genie in a Bottle" marked the third time that year that a new female artist reached number one on the Hot 100 with her debut single [3]. The song was widely recognized as one of Aguilera's signature songs, and it was featured heavily on MTV's "Total Request Live" [5].

The second season of Jessica Jones began streaming on Netflix on March 8, 2018 [1][4]. This release date was announced in December 2017, with a teaser trailer being released at the same time [1]. The series is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe and was produced by Marvel Television in association with ABC Studios and Tall Girls Productions [5].

The end of Roman rule in Britain was marked by a series of events that took place in the 5th century AD. The Romano-Britons, who were the indigenous population living under Roman rule, took charge of their own affairs after a local revolt in approximately 410 [1][2]. The Romans themselves left Britain in response to changes in their priorities and needs [1][5].

During the 2012 Summer Olympics opening ceremony, the torch was lit by a team of seven young athletes, each one nominated by a famous British Olympian [1][2][4]. The identity of the athlete who would light the cauldron was kept secret until the event [1].

The Latin word "camera obscura" (plural "camera obscura" or "camera obscuras"; from Latin, meaning "dark room": "camera" "(vaulted) chamber or room," and "obscura" "dark") refers to a natural optical phenomenon that occurs when an image of a scene at the other side of a screen is projected through a small hole in that screen as a reversed and inverted image (left to right and upside down) on a surface opposite to the opening [1][2][3][4] To create a simple camera obscura, one can use a box, tracing paper, tape, foil, a box cutter, a pencil, and a blanket to keep out the light [3]. The term "camera obscura" also refers to constructions or devices that make use of this principle within a box, tent, or room [4]. The camera obscura box was developed further into the photographic camera in the first half of the 19th century [4]. The name "camera lucida" (Latin for "light chamber") is obviously intended to recall the much older drawing aid, the "camera obscura" (Latin for "dark chamber"), but it has no optical similarity with the camera obscura [5].
The most games the Red Sox have won in a season was 105, in the 1912 season [3]. The team additionally set a new franchise record for wins in a season with 108 in the 2018 season [2].

The winner of Britain's Got Talent 2015 was Jules O'Dwyer & Matisse [1]. This series was aired between April 11 and May 31, 2015 [3]. However, viewers complained about being misled by the winner's performance as it was found that their act involved a second dog that had not been disclosed to the public or the judges [1].

The East IndiaCompany, which traded in India since 1639, was the means by which cricket was introduced into India. The earliest reference to cricket being played in the Indian sub-continent is dated 1721 when British sailors of the East India Company were playing the game at Cambay, near Baroda [2][3]. Henry Tonge, a member of a British mission at Aleppo in the Ottoman Empire (now in Syria), in 1676 is the earliest known mention of cricket being played outside England, confirming that cricket was already played in India as well [2]. The Parsi community in Mumbai (formerly Bombay) established the Oriental Cricket Clubin 1848, and the Parsis are credited with starting cricket in India as they were in close contacts with the Imperial British due to their interests in trade [4].
Matt Brody was played by David Charvet [1] on the original television series "Baywatch." In the 2017 film adaptation, Matt Brody is a character but it is not clear who played this role.

The Black Stallion in the book series and film by Walter Farley is described as an Arab stallion [2][3]. In the book series, the Black Stallion is later given several offspring, including a colt named Satan, but the horse's original breed is not discussed [2]. In the 1979 film, the horse is played by a real horse known as Cass Ole, which is an Arabian stallion [3]. The Phantom Stallion, a horse that appears in a separate work with no relation to the Black Stallion, is described as being half Quarter Horse and Half Mustang [1].

The most common type of rock in Earth's crust is igneous rock, which makes up about 64.7% of the Earth's crust by volume [1]. The oceanic crust is primarily composed of basalt, a type of igneous rock of mafic composition [2]. Overall, igneous rocks account for about 90-95% of the top 16 km of the Earth's crust by volume [3]. The continental crust, which is thicker than the oceanic crust, is primarily composed of sodium potassium aluminium silicate rocks, including granite [2].

Instead, he invited Mickey Thomas, a background singer in his band at the time, to sing it. The song peaked at #3 on the "Billboard" Hot 100 singles chart in May 1976 [1, 2].

The song "As Time Goes By" was written by Herman Hupfeld in 1931 [1]. It became famous in 1942 when part of it was sung by the character Sam (Dooley Wilson) in the movie "Casablanca" [1][3]. The song has since been used in various film and television soundtracks [1][3][5].

A systolic blood pressure value is the pressure measurement in the arteries when the ventricles are contracting near the end of the cardiac cycle [1][2][3]. This occurs at a peak pressure, noted as the systolic blood pressure when using a sphygmomanometer to measure blood pressure [4][5]. A normal measured value for a resting, healthy adult human is 120 mmHg systolic [1][2][3][5].

"There Will Be Blood" is a film that takes place in Southern California during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, specifically during the oil boom [2]. "Brave Blood" takes place in the home of a psychiatrist who takes in a group of female prostitutes in order to help better their lives [1].

In the first telecast of Monday Night Football on September 21, 1970, the Cleveland Browns defeated the New York Jets [3]. Specifically, the Browns won 31–21 [4]. The first NFL game for the Jets, including this Monday Night Football broadcast, was in 1970 following the league merger [1].

The New England Patriots have won three consecutive Super Bowl championships once, during the 2003-2004 seasons [1][2][3]. However, they have not managed to win more than three in row since then [4][5].

In networking, NAT stands for Network Address Translation. It is a method used to remap one IP address space into another by modifying network address information in packets as they transit across a traffic routing device [1][2][3]. The aim is to conserve global address space in the face of IPv4 address exhaustion. One Internet-routable IP address of a NAT gateway can be used for an entire private network [1].

The third How to Train Your Dragon movie is called How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World and was released on February 22, 2019 [2]. The release date had been moved several times, with initial plans for a 2016 release followed by changes to 2017, 2018, and eventually 2019 [3][4][5]. The first trailer for the movie was released in June 2018 [2].

"I'm Not Gonna Miss You" was written by Glen Campbell and Julian Raymond [1][2]. The song is featured in the documentary "Glen Campbell: I'll Be Me" and was nominated for Best Original Song at the 87th Academy Awards [1][2][3]. It was also the last song recorded by Campbell.

In the film adaptation of How the Grinch Stole Christmas, Cindy Lou Who is played by actress Taylor Momsen [1]. Emily Grace Reaves may be known for playing Cindy Lou in a different project [3]. Cindy Carol, an actress who was born on October 11, 1944, is credited for playing Cindy Lou in a film titled Gidget Goes to Rome [2], but it is not clear which version of the character she plays in this film. Additionally, there is a Carmen Jones movie where Olga James plays Cindy Lou [4], but it is unclear if this is a different character named Cindy Lou or the same character from other productions.

The ribeye steak comes from the rib section of a cow, specifically the area spanning from ribs six through twelve [1][2][3][4]. In the United States, the term rib eye steak typically refers to the steak with the bone removed [1][3]. In Australia and New Zealand, the cut served with the bone is called "ribeye" and with the bone removed it is called "Scotch fillet" [3].

The Lion King debuted on Broadway at the New Amsterdam Theater on October 15, 1997 [1][4] with previews, before officially opening on November 13, 1997 [1][4]. The show is still running in New York after more than 8,500 performances [1]. The musical is also still running in the West End [2] and has been one of the most successful in Broadway history, winning six Tony Awards including Best Musical [4].

The Golden State Warriors are based in Oakland, California [1][3][4]. They play their home games at the Oracle Arena [1][2]. The team's relocation to the San Francisco Bay Area took place in 1962 [4]. Prior to the 1971–72 season, the franchise changed its geographic moniker to Golden State to suggest representing the entire state of California [3].

The composition for the film How to Train Your Dragon was written by John Powell [1][3][4]. He collaborated with Icelandic singer Jónsi who wrote and performed the song "Sticks & Stones" for the film [4].

The first man-made object to enter space was a German V-2 rocket on a vertical test flight on October 3, 1942 [2], although the German A-4 rocket had already reached an altitude of 11 km before exploding in a previous launch in March 1942 [2]. Earlier, on March 16, 1926, American scientist Robert Goddard launched the world's first liquid-fueled rocket in Auburn, Massachusetts, reaching an altitude of 41 feet and a distance of 184 feet [4]. The highest known projectile prior to the rockets of the 1940s were the shells of the Paris Gun, which reached at least 40 kilometers altitude during World War One [5].

Hungry Jack's, a franchise of Burger King Corporation, operates approximately 390 stores in Australia, according to Document [2], [3], and [4]. As mentioned in Document [1] and [5], Competitive Foods Australia, Hungry Jack's parent company, also owns 50 KFC outlets in Western Australia and the Northern Territory.

The song "You Know Better Than I" is sung by David Campbell in the 2000 direct-to-video film Joseph: King of Dreams [1][2][3]. The song expresses Joseph's trust in God's plan for him even when things seem difficult [2][3]. The film's signature song has been praised for its spirituality and deeper message compared to similar songs in other films [4][5].

The song "If I Were a Boy" was originally written by BC Jean and Toby Gad [1][2][3][4][5]. Jean, who initially wanted to keep the song for her own album, later expressed her frustration when Beyoncé was set to release it as a single. Despite her initial upset, the two eventually reached a deal, with Beyoncé promising to record a duet with Jean for her debut album.

"10 Things I Hate About You" is set in the Seattle metropolitan area, with many scenes filmed at Stadium High School in Tacoma [1][3][4]. The film's story is a modernization of William Shakespeare's play, "The Taming of the Shrew," and is set in an American high school setting [2].

In association football (soccer), substitutions are generally made during stoppages in play and with the referee's permission, with a maximum of three substitutions per team allowed during regular play, and an additional substitution allowed if the game goes into extra-time [1][3][4]. Unlike some other sports, a player who has been substituted during a match may not re-enter it [3]. In certain competitions and friendly matches, the number of permitted substitutions may vary [4].

Guadalupe Peak, located in Guadalupe Mountains National Park, is the highest natural point in Texas, with an elevation of above sea level [1]. This peak is significantly higher than the Franklin Mountains in El Paso, the highest point of which is North Franklin Mountain at 7,192 feet [2].

The book An Essay on the Principle of Population was first published anonymously in 1798, with the author soon identified as Thomas Robert Malthus [1]. The book, which is considered the most influential work on population of its era [1], was primarily concerned with predicting that population would increase geometrically, doubling every 25 years, but food production would only grow arithmetically, which would result in famine and starvation, unless births were controlled [1, 4]. Malthus's book fueled debate about the size of population and the need for population control [1, 4].

Bruce Springsteen performed at the Super Bowl halftime show during Super Bowl XLIII [3]. This performance took place on February 1, 2009 [1]. Springsteen had turned down numerous Super Bowl performance invitations before this event, understanding its prestige value and finally accepting [1].
Season 1 of Sherlock consists of three 90-minute episodes [1]. The series has a total of thirteen episodes across four series, with no episodes in Season 2 [4].

The movie The Summer of 42 was filmed on Nantucket Island, off the coast of Cape Cod [2]. According to a Variety report from July 2, 1975, the locations for the movie included Greenwood, MS and other local communities [1]. Some interior scenes were shot in Atlanta Film Studios Paulding County in Hiram, Georgia, and most of the interior stadium shots were filmed at Engel Stadium in Chattanooga, Tennessee [4]. There is no information provided in the documents regarding whether the movie was filmed in any other locations.

The Portuguese called the region that we now know as Mumbai by the name "Bombaim," which possibly originated as the Galician-Portuguese phrase "bom baim," meaning "good little bay" [3]. The name was first used by Portuguese writer Gaspar Correia in his "Lendas da Índia" ("Legends of India") in 1508 [4]. The Portuguese also called it "Tana-Maiambu" in 1516, where "Tana" appears to refer to the adjoining town of Thane and "Maiambu" to "Mumbadevi" [4]. Other variations recorded in the 16th and 17th centuries include "Mombayn," "Bombay," "Bombain," "Bombaym," "Monbaym," "Mombaim," "Mombaiim," and "Bambaye" [4].

In the TV series Still Game, Winston moves to an exterior set in the Glasgow North Media Park, Maryhill, after the owner of the pub where he usually meets his friends demolishes the building [1]. The character Winston Place, who shares a similar name, lived in Rawtenstall in Lancashire and played cricket [2]. However, the TV character Winston does not appear to have any connection to the real person Winston Place or the cricketer.

The ratio of the wave height to its wave length is called the significant wave height (SWH or "H"). It is defined as the mean wave height (trough to crest) of the highest third of the waves [1][2][3][4]. The SWH is generally well approximated by a Rayleigh distribution, and statistically, one might encounter a wave that is roughly double the significant wave height [2][3]. Other statistical measures of the wave height are also used [4].

The Knicks won their last NBA championship in 1973 [1]. They reclaimed the title in a 4-1 series against the Los Angeles Lakers, with Walter Frazier playing a key role in the defense against NBA superstar Jerry West [2]. The Knicks have not made it back to the NBA Finals since then [1].

The two theme parks at Euro Disney are Disneyland Park and Walt Disney Studios Park [1][2][3]. These parks are part of Disneyland Paris, which is an entertainment resort located east of Paris, France [1][3]. Unlike Europa-Park, which is the largest theme park in Germany and the second most popular in Europe, Euro Disney is owned and operated by The Walt Disney Company [1].

During the 1890s, ragtime music began to become popular in the United States and reached widespread popularity in the latter part of the 19th century [1][2][3]. For at least 12 years after its publication, "Maple Leaf Rag" heavily influenced subsequent ragtime composers with its melody lines, harmonic progressions or metric patterns [4]. The music style was characterized by its unique syncopation and was popularized by composers such as Scott Joplin [4][5].

The men's figure skating competition at the 2018 Winter Olympics was held on 16 and 17 February 2018 in Gangneung, South Korea [1]. The short program was held on 16 February and the free skating was held on 17 February [1]. With his victory at the competition, Yuzuru Hanyu of Japan became the first male figure skater to win two consecutive gold medals [1].

The Philadelphia Phillies won the World Series in 1980, defeating the Kansas City Royals in game 6 on Oct. 21, 1980 [1][2][3]. The Phillies advanced all the way to the World Series after winning the National League East title in the regular season and defeating the Houston Astros in the NLCS [1][3]. Their victory in 1980 brought an end to the stigma of the 1964 "Phold" and made them the first championship-winning team in Philadelphia since the 1983 NBA Finals [4]. In the 2008 season, the Phillies won their second championship in their 126-year history [5].

On the TV show Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman, Ingrid was played by Jessica Bowman starting in the third season after the original portrayer, Erika Flores, did not renew her contract [1][4][5]. Before Bowman, Ingrid was played by Ashley Jones [1].

The process of transcribing a gene from DNA to RNA in cells is called transcription [1][2][3]. The resulting RNA molecule is known as messenger RNA (mRNA) [1]. During transcription, a DNA-dependent RNA polymerase is responsible for copying the gene sequence into an mRNA transcript [2][3].

The third season of RuPaul's Drag Race All Stars premiered on January 25, 2018, as announced by VH1 on December 14, 2017 [1]. The season featured ten returning contestants competing to be inducted into the Drag Race Hall of Fame [2][3].

Piper Chapman, the protagonist in the Netflix series Orange Is the New Black, is played by Taylor Schilling [2][3][4]. This character is based on Piper Kerman, author of the non-fiction book "Orange Is the New Black", upon which the series is based [2]. Kerman spent 13 months in a federal correctional facility for money-laundering activities [1].

The first commercially available cellular phone was the Motorola DynaTAC, developed by a team led by Martin Cooper, a former general manager for the systems division at Motorola [2][3]. Cooper is credited with making the first mobile phone call from a handheld subscriber equipment in 1973 [4]. The Motorola DynaTAC was released to consumers in the USA in 1983 [3]. [1]

In the film The Sound of Music, the family von Trapp escape to Switzerland after fleeing the Austrian border [1]. The final scene shows the family hiking on the Obersalzberg near the German town of Berchtesgaden, within sight of Adolf Hitler's Kehlsteinhaus Eagle's Nest retreat [1][3][4]. In reality, the family simply walked to the local train station and boarded a train to Italy [4].

This revelation was met with an average weekly audience of 7.1 million "live" viewers in the UK, peaking at 9.3 million viewers during the final episode [3]. The reveal did not have the same success in the US, only averaging 4.7 million viewers per episode on BBC America [5]. The first series began airing in the UK on March 4, 2013 and was based on a story that creator Chris Chibnall began fleshing out in 2011 [4].

Argentina has won the FIFA World Cup twice, first in 1978, beating the Netherlands 3-1 [1][4], and second in 1986, with a 3-2 victory over West Germany [1][4]. These victories were under coaches César Luis Menotti in 1978 and Carlos Bilardo in 1986 [4]. Argentina has also been runners-up in the World Cup three times [1][4]: in 1930, 1990, and 2014. According to the documents provided, Argentina is not mentioned as winners of the FIFA World Cup in other years than 1978 and 1986.
